title: HEDIS Core DocumentReference
description: The HEDIS Core DocumentReference profile extends the US Core requirements to include requirements for measure calculation.

element.definition: [HEDIS] The metadata about a resource. This is content in the resource that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.
[US Core] Other identifiers associated with the document, including version independent identifiers.
[US Core] The status of this document reference.
[US Core] Specifies the particular kind of document referenced  (e.g. History and Physical, Discharge Summary, Progress Note). This usually equates to the purpose of making the document referenced.
[US Core] A categorization for the type of document referenced - helps for indexing and searching. This may be implied by or derived from the code specified in the DocumentReference.type.

[HEDIS][US Core] Who or what the document is about. The document can be about a person, (patient or healthcare practitioner), a device (e.g. a machine) or even a group of subjects (such as a document about a herd of farm animals, or a set of patients that share a common exposure).
[US Core] When the document reference was created.
[US Core] Identifies who is responsible for adding the information to the document.
[US Core] Identifies the organization or group who is responsible for ongoing maintenance of and access to the document.
[US Core] The document and format referenced. There may be multiple content element repetitions, each with a different format.
[US Core] The document or URL of the document along with critical metadata to prove content has integrity.
[US Core] Identifies the type of the data in the attachment and allows a method to be chosen to interpret or render the data. Includes mime type parameters such as charset where appropriate.
[US Core] The actual data of the attachment - a sequence of bytes, base64 encoded.
[US Core] A location where the data can be accessed.
[US Core] An identifier of the document encoding, structure, and template that the document conforms to beyond the base format indicated in the mimeType.
[US Core] The clinical context in which the document was prepared.
[US Core] Describes the clinical encounter or type of care that the document content is associated with.
[US Core] The time period over which the service that is described by the document was provided.
